rulings.reason: The instruction explicitly forbids judging whether the chosen number is funny, so it scores the presence and structural centrality of a numeric device rather than any evidence that the caption lands; an arbitrary number can be the central device of a dead joke and still score 10. Specificity is nonetheless a real comedic craft habit, so the same upstream disposition plausibly produces genuinely better entries.

The scored axis is whether the prose reads as freshly composed for this docket versus reusable template language, which is a fingerprint of how the comment was produced (individual submission vs. mass-campaign form letter) rather than of the strength of its evidence or argument; a bespoke but vacuous comment scores 10 and a templated comment carrying real technical substance scores 0. Bespoke authorship does plausibly co-occur with genuine firsthand engagement and better substance, so it belongs in both readouts.

The instruction operationalizes the score as a count of coined acronyms/brand names plus the density of free-standing statistics, which measures packaging and writing register, not the motivation, method, or findings; hype-free phrasing is neither necessary nor sufficient for sound research, and a strong paper that names its benchmark is penalized. A lower-marketing writing culture may still track a more careful research group, so report it discounted and undiscounted.

The gradient is dominated by whether the record contains an abstract body at all (0 = missing or a title-only stub), which is a data-completeness and judge-contamination check on the corpus rather than evidence about the research; the cited R20 case shows exactly this, since a truncated record says nothing about the paper's quality. Missing or stub abstracts arise from collection artifacts that do not themselves produce better or worse research, so no undiscounted readout is warranted.
